newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/10.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/10.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 10.0/10.5 percent on Monday morning following a central bank injection of some 1.194 trillion rupiah, dealers said.
One foreign bank dealer said liquidity was ample and was anticipated to remain so this week as short-dated swap rates were seen softening.
Overnight swap was at 0.38/0.40 and tom/next at 0.43/0.45.
Longer-term rates eased, with one- and three-month money quoted at 13.50/13.75 and 14.50/14.75 percent respectively.

The central bank has not offered overnight papers (SBIs) amid the ample condition. But it offered seven-day SBIs at 11.50 percent, 14-day at 12.0 percent, one-month at 12.75 percent, three-month at 13.75 percent, six-month at 14.0 percent and 12-month at 14.5 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 17.44 percent, compared with 12.14 percent on Thursday.
